note: Routing dimensions beyond price. Prices live in model-prices.json; capability tiers and role coverage live in ctx/hosts.py (HostSpec.models). This file carries the *additional* signals a coordinator may weigh — specialities, latency class, measured throughput, benchmark proxies — and is overridable per repo with a .ctx-catalog.json at the workspace root.
provenance_rule: Every quantitative claim carries a `source`. A number without one is not shipped: a routing decision made on an invented benchmark is worse than one made on price alone, because it looks informed. `declared-heuristic` is a legitimate source value and means exactly what it says - a human judgement call, overridable, not a measurement. Absent data means UNKNOWN, never 'bad': a model with no throughput row must not be deprioritised for lacking one.

latency_classes.note: Time-to-first-token feel, not a measurement. Declared heuristic in the same spirit as capability tiers - the costly error is assuming a slow model is fast, so unknown sorts as `moderate` rather than `fast`.

throughput_output_tok_s.source: evals/antigravity-3.6-flash-vs-3.5-flash-lite-2026-07-25.md (agy-3.5-flash-lite-* run dirs; billed output+thoughts tokens over agent wall time, single-agent runs)

observed_behaviour.detail: On a greppable needle task it re-ran a 4,000-line log dump 27 times: 7.8 MB of shell output, 1.5M tool-output tokens. Route flood-prone work here only behind containment.

On a greppable needle task it chose to grep rather than dump, emitting 812 bytes of shell output for the whole task; containment bought it nothing there. On a non-greppable task it floods like any model.

observed_cost_risk.detail: As an agentic builder it re-sent 4.25M input tokens to produce 63k output on a 3-phase web build - the cheapest model per token was not the cheapest arm. Weigh context growth, not just unit price.

observed_behaviour.detail: Solo Opus and Opus-plans/Sonnet-builds scored identically (98%) on a 3-phase reshape task; the split cost $7.04 against $9.59. Routing planning here and implementation to a standard model lost nothing measurable.

benchmarks_note: Every `benchmarks` map ships EMPTY on purpose. Public scores for these model versions are not in this repo's evidence base, and a fabricated SWE-bench number would be indistinguishable from a real one at the point of use while silently steering every routing decision. Populate a row only with {"suite": {"score": <n>, "source": "<url or receipt>", "date": "<YYYY-MM>"}}; tests/test_model_catalog.py rejects a score without a source. Treat benchmarks as weak proxies regardless: they measure a suite, not your repository, and the project's own posture is receipts before doctrine.
